hints.title: State Formulation
hints.text: At each station, track the minimum cost to arrive on the regular lane and on the express lane.

hints.title: Express Lane Transitions
hints.text: Switching from regular to express lane costs expressCost plus express[i]. Switching from express to regular is free.

hints.title: Station by Station Dynamic Programming
hints.text: Compute regular cost as min(reg + r, exp + r) and express cost as min(exp + e, reg + expressCost + e).

hints.title: Two State Dynamic Programming Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def minimumCosts(self, regular: list[int], express: list[int], expressCost: int) -> list[int]:
        dp_reg = 0
        dp_exp = expressCost
        ans = []
        for r, e in zip(regular, express):
            new_reg = min(dp_reg + r, dp_exp + r)
            new_exp = min(dp_exp + e, dp_reg + expressCost + e)
            dp_reg, dp_exp = new_reg, new_exp
            ans.append(min(dp_reg, dp_exp))
        return ans
```

complexity.notes: Single pass updating two scalar states.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Brute force branching across lanes at every stop causes exponential 2^n paths.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Rolling scalar registers replace full DP tables.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Models multi-track transit as a two-state Markov decision DP.
